Put a depth record on a regular time grid, filling short gaps

Source: R/regularise_archive.R
regularise_archive.Rd

regularise_archive() puts a depth record on a regular time grid, so that each record is the same time apart, as the wavelet analysis assumes. It is run by import_tag_data(), so imported records are already regular.

Usage

regularise_archive(
  archive,
  interval_s = NULL,
  max_fill_mins = 5,
  min_coverage = 70,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

archive

A depth record: a data frame with a POSIXct 'date' column, a numeric 'depth' column and, optionally, a 'temp' column, such as from import_tag_data(). Its 'time_zone' attribute sets the days.

interval_s

The sampling interval of the grid in seconds. NULL (the default) uses the record's most common interval.

max_fill_mins

The longest gap, in minutes, to fill by interpolation for analysis (default 5). At most 360 (6 hours). 0 fills no gaps.

min_coverage

The percentage of a day's records that must be real (not filled) for the day to be analysed (default 70).

verbose

Print a summary.

Value

The record on the regular grid: a data frame with 'date', 'depth', 'temp' (if present), 'date_only', and the logical columns 'filled' (interpolated) and 'long_gap' (filled only for the wavelet). Its attributes are:

  • time_zone, interval_s, max_fill_mins and min_coverage

  • day_coverage: for each day, its real records, expected records, percentage coverage, and whether it is kept for analysis

  • gaps: each gap's start and end (the records either side), length in seconds, missing records, and whether it was filled for analysis

  • sampling_report: the sampling_report() of the records before they were put on the grid

Details

The grid runs from local midnight on the first day to midnight after the last record, every interval_s seconds, in step with the first record so that real records keep their times. Each grid time takes the nearest record within half an interval. Duplicate times, times out of order and records sampled at other rates are resolved this way.

Grid times with no record are gaps, filled by linear interpolation between the records either side:

  • Short gaps, up to max_fill_mins long (from one record to the next), are filled and used in the analysis, with a warning.

  • Longer gaps, and any time before the first or after the last record, are filled only so that the wavelet can run, and marked in the long_gap column. create_depth_stats() leaves them out, and create_wavelet_stats() leaves out the wavelet power near them.

Each day's coverage is the percentage of its grid times that have a real record. Days with less than min_coverage are left out of the wavelet and depth statistics. A day with a filled gap of 6 hours has 75% coverage.

See also

sampling_report() to check a record's sampling.

Examples

archive_days <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "data", "archive_days.rds", package = "FishDiveR"))

# Remove a few records to make two gaps
gappy <- archive_days[-c(100:102, 5000:5300), ]
regular <- suppressWarnings(regularise_archive(gappy, max_fill_mins = 5))

attr(regular, "gaps")
#>                 start                 end length_s missing_records filled
#> 1 2000-01-01 01:38:00 2000-01-01 01:42:00      240               3   TRUE
#> 2 2000-01-04 11:18:00 2000-01-04 16:20:00    18120             301  FALSE
head(attr(regular, "day_coverage"))
#>         date records expected coverage kept
#> 1 2000-01-01    1437     1440    99.79 TRUE
#> 2 2000-01-02    1440     1440   100.00 TRUE
#> 3 2000-01-03    1440     1440   100.00 TRUE
#> 4 2000-01-04    1139     1440    79.10 TRUE
#> 5 2000-01-05    1440     1440   100.00 TRUE
#> 6 2000-01-06    1440     1440   100.00 TRUE
